cards.power: Asset Freeze: Target player cannot draw cards next turn. They are auditing their hoard.
cards.lore: He sat on the gold until Loki squeezed him like a stress ball. It's not hoarding if you're underground.
cards.gradeReason: Clear character but power reads mechanical before the personality kicks in.

cards.power: Forced Liquidation: Steal a card from an opponent. If they complain, steal another.
cards.lore: He caught the pike, killed the otter, and enslaved the dwarf. Basically, a standard consultant.
cards.gradeReason: "If they complain, steal another" — you know exactly how to play this character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval illumination. Subject: smug fox in consultant suit stealing from others. Mood: gleefully amoral.

cards.power: Compound Interest: The holder gains +2 Attack but must discard a card every turn. The debt always wins.
cards.lore: Andvaranaut. It breeds gold, but it eats owners. The ultimate pyramid scheme.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic IS the curse — the player lives the trap. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Norse rune art. Subject: golden cursed ring with serpent devouring its tail. Mood: ominous cycle.

cards.power: Bad Ending: Attach to a Hero Card. That Hero dies at the end of the round. No saves.
cards.lore: Death to the owner. Joy to no one. Until the gold returns to the water everyone is just renting their life.
cards.gradeReason: "No saves" lands like a gavel. The lore is a one-sentence cosmology.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: aged parchment decree. Subject: unrolling scroll with wax skull seal and red fine print. Mood: doomed.

cards.power: Main Character Syndrome: You cannot lose a duel unless the opponent is literally a god.
cards.lore: Strong enough to kill a dragon. Dumb enough to not check his blind spot. The ultimate himbo.
cards.gradeReason: "The ultimate himbo" + Main Character Syndrome = instant character read at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: epic illustration. Subject: buff golden retriever in dragon-scale armor flexing heroically. Mood: obliviously invincible.

cards.power: Thick Skin: Ignore all damage from non-magical weapons. You smell great. You are legally invincible.
cards.lore: Bathe in the blood of your enemies — it's great for your skin. Also great for people who don't moisturize.
cards.gradeReason: Strong concept but lore partially obscured at this resolution; power is clear and playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vivid fantasy. Subject: golden retriever bathing in black dragon-blood cauldron. Mood: triumphant self-care.

cards.power: Critical Fall: Play on an opponent's Hero Card. Their Defense drops to 0.
cards.lore: One tiny leaf. The giant design flaw. Every great hero hates perfection.
cards.gradeReason: Instant comprehension: you find the one weakness, you drop it, done.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: close-up botanical. Subject: tiny leaf on hero's back forming crosshair target. Mood: design flaw revealed.

cards.power: Overkill: +4 Attack, but if this kills the target, destroys opponent's weapon card too.
cards.lore: Subtlety is for people who can't cleave an anvil in half.
cards.gradeReason: "Subtlety is for people who can't cleave an anvil in half" — play this card like you mean it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heroic fantasy. Subject: massive sword splitting anvil in courtyard with sparks flying. Mood: spectacular overkill.

cards.power: Delegate Authority: When challenged, force another player to fight for you.
cards.lore: King of Burgundy. Brave leader, as long as someone else is doing the fighting, wooing, and thinking.
cards.gradeReason: "Delegate Authority" is an immediately playable personality: the king who outsources everything.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical portrait. Subject: crowned sheep with scepter looking pompous and oblivious. Mood: cowardly dignity.

cards.power: Assist Mode: Add Siegfried's Attack stats to Gunther's roll. Invisible cheating is still cheating.
cards.lore: Invisibility cloak. Great for wrestling women who are stronger than you without them knowing. Creepy.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic requires knowing the Siegfried card link; works but needs table context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ghostly medieval. Subject: checkered invisibility cloak floating in stone corridor. Mood: creepy deception.

cards.power: Identity Theft: Swap hand cards with another player. Claim it was a misunderstanding.
cards.lore: He stands there, she fights him. He takes the credit. The original deepfake technology.
cards.gradeReason: "Claim it was a misunderstanding" — you know the face to make when you play this.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval comedy. Subject: armored sheep gesturing while retriever battles polar bear for him. Mood: audacious fraud.

cards.power: Travel Montage: Skip a turn to draw 3 cards.
cards.lore: A long voyage to find a woman who can kill you with a pebble. Men are idiots.
cards.gradeReason: Good setup card; lore is funny but doesn't give a performative role beyond waiting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Norse epic. Subject: Viking longship with sheep and fox sailing through ominous seas. Mood: doomed optimism.

cards.power: Gatekeeper: Challenge an incoming player. If they lose, they are eliminated from the game.
cards.lore: Queen of Iceland. Throws boulders for fun. Virginity is her power source (allegedly).
cards.gradeReason: "Throws boulders for fun" — instant embodiment. The gatekeeper role plays itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Norse warrior. Subject: fierce polar bear queen in armor hurling massive boulder. Mood: formidable and magnificent.

cards.power: Heavy Artillery: Deal 5 damage. If the target is 'Gunther', deal 10.
cards.lore: If you can't lift this, don't ask for her hand.
cards.gradeReason: "If target is Gunther, deal 10" — that conditional triggers immediate roleplay at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action illustration. Subject: massive boulder mid-flight over Viking competition ground. Mood: devastating and inevitable.

cards.power: Shield Breaker: Ignore opponent's Defense stats this turn.
cards.lore: It went through the shield, the armor, and the ego. Gunther fainted watching it.
cards.gradeReason: Strong lore but A-stat obscured at this resolution; mechanic is straightforward removal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: athletic medieval. Subject: massive spear piercing layered shields and armor in competition. Mood: unstoppable force.

cards.power: Time Out: Suspend an opponent's Hero card for one round. They cannot act.
cards.lore: She tied the King up and hung him on the wall until morning. The most honest interaction in the whole saga.
cards.gradeReason: "The most honest interaction in the whole saga" — you drop this card knowing exactly what you're doing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark comedy. Subject: crowned sheep dangling from castle wall hook looking humiliated. Mood: power dynamics clarified.

cards.power: Tag Team: Play this card to double your Attack for one turn, then lose 2 Health.
cards.lore: The lights went out, and the 'King' suddenly got very strong. Kayfabe at its finest.
cards.gradeReason: "Kayfabe at its finest" — meta self-awareness that rewards players who know what they're doing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval sports. Subject: polar bear pinning sheep in darkened chamber, retriever's shadow nearby. Mood: rigged contest.

cards.power: Disempower: Target loses all special abilities. Without the belt, the magic is gone.
cards.lore: Steal it as a souvenir. Proof of conquest. Also, proof of being a terrible brother-in-law.
cards.gradeReason: Good mechanic, clear role but more inventory move than performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ornate medieval. Subject: glowing magical belt on stone pedestal, shadow of thieving hand. Mood: power stripped.

cards.power: Evidence: Reveal this card to start a war between two players.
cards.lore: He gave the other woman's ring to his wife. Rookie mistake. Tactical suicide.
cards.gradeReason: "Reveal this card to start a war" — no description needed. Drop it and watch the table explode.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dramatic medieval. Subject: two queens confronting each other, gold ring visible between them. Mood: powder keg.

cards.power: Depower: Change Brunhild's stats to 1/1/1.
cards.lore: Once she lost her virginity, she lost her strength. Ancient writers really didn't understand how women work.
cards.gradeReason: Describes a stat change and invites source commentary — player has nothing to embody or perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tragic medieval. Subject: polar bear queen kneeling, power visibly draining away into stone floor. Mood: diminished.

cards.power: Pragmatism: Cancel any 'Magic' or 'Lore' effect played against you. Reality checks hurt.
cards.lore: He's not a villain. He's the only guy in the story who actually does his job. Digs holes, buries bodies.
cards.gradeReason: "Digs holes, buries bodies" — the entire character in four words. Play this card like you're right.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gritty medieval. Subject: armored badger with calculating eyes in torchlit hall. Mood: pragmatic menace entirely justified.

cards.power: Marked for Death: Attach to Siegfried. Attacks against him gain +5 Damage.
cards.lore: Kriemhild sewed it on to 'protect' him. Hagen used it as a bullseye. Loose lips sink ships.
cards.gradeReason: "Loose lips sink ships" reframes a wife's love as tactical intelligence failure. Devastating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ominous medieval. Subject: red cross stitched on golden retriever's back viewed from behind. Mood: betrayal embroidered in.

cards.power: Distraction: Force opponents to tap out/rest their strongest card for a turn.

cards.power: Trauma: Target opponent must discard their hand due to grief.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark medieval. Subject: body dropped on castle doorstep at dawn, crown visible nearby. Mood: calculated cruelty as communication.

cards.power: Horde Command: Summon 3 'Hun' tokens (1/1/1) to fight for you.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Hunnic epic. Subject: massive ox-king in gilded armor on throne, surrounded by small warriors. Mood: powerful but manipulated.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grim aftermath. Subject: old wolf standing over fallen queen looking profoundly disturbed. Mood: chivalry as broken logic.

cards.power: Mourning: Skip 3 turns. Contemplate existence.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: melancholic epic. Subject: lion and ox weeping over ruins of mead-hall at grey dawn. Mood: hollow victory, empty hall.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ouroboros fantasy. Subject: serpent dragon in Nibelung armor swallowing its own tail. Mood: eternal reboot.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: meta cartoon. Subject: cartoon rabbit holding scissors over game board grinning at viewer. Mood: fourth-wall fully dissolved.

cards.power: Ego Boost: +8 Attack, but you cannot retreat or heal. Ever.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical epic. Subject: antlered warrior charging forward ignoring multiple wounds and warnings. Mood: unstoppable self-destruction.

cards.power: Narrative Necessity: You cannot die until act 5.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: meta fantasy. Subject: knight surrounded by glowing narrative-force shield, arrows bouncing off. Mood: script as armor.

cards.power: Weltschmerz: All players lose 1 morale token.
cards.lore: It's not about winning. It's about enduring the inevitable doom with a stoic face.
cards.gradeReason: Culturally perfect; but the role is "lose morale stoically" — more condition than character.

cards.power: Wildcard: Assign any value to this card.

cards.gradeReason: "Assign any value" makes the player the narrator. The card names what all the other cards were chasing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: meta prop design. Subject: plain cardboard box labeled IMPORTANT PLOT DEVICE on empty pedestal. Mood: knowing and inevitable.

verdict: The Nibelungen Booster hits like a spear in the back — which is exactly where you weren't looking. Every card nails the core principle: Gunther delegates his own courtship, Hagen buries bodies and gets called a villain for it, and Toxic Masculinity is literally the +8 Attack card you can never retreat from. Weakness: The Submission flattens Brunhild's arc to a stat drop without giving the player anything to do. Named strength: the consistent animal character design (retriever, badger, polar bear, sheep) makes every face instantly readable at table distance. Table-ready Y.
blurb: The Germanic epic where everyone dies, the gold stays lost forever, and Hagen was correct the entire time. 60 cards distilling the entire Nibelungenlied into table chaos — from Brunhild's boulder throw to Kriemhild's very committed hall-burning revenge plan.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: NIBELUNGEN – The Germanic Epic Where Everyone Dies and Hagen Was Right (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Eight hundred years before anyone filmed a Red Wedding, a German poet sat down and killed every single guest at the party.

The Nibelungenlied is the original body count. Siegfried the golden retriever himbo takes a spear in the one spot he should never have mentioned. Gunther the sheep delegates his own courtship to a stronger man and spends the rest of the poem pretending he won. Brunhild the polar bear gets cheated out of a fair fight, and Kriemhild burns down a hall full of people to balance the ledger. Everyone calls Hagen the badger the villain, mostly because he was the only one doing the math out loud. The gold goes into the Rhine and stays there. Nobody learns anything, which is the most honest thing about it.

So you take Siegfried, perform the invincible hero with a straight face, and the table decides whether the bit survives the spot on his back he forgot to flag. That is the whole game.
